explanation: The statement is about the library's own definitions: `SymplecticForm` (TauCeti/Geometry/Symplectic/AlmostComplex.lean), its `toBilinForm`, the associated `toContinuousBilinearMap.inverse` (TauCeti/Geometry/Symplectic/Duality.lean) and `hamiltonianVectorField` (Basic.lean). I searched Mathlib for `hamiltonianVectorField`, `Hamiltonian`, `symplectic`, and `SymplecticForm`: Mathlib has only Hamiltonian *graphs* (Combinatorics/SimpleGraph/Hamiltonian.lean), the symplectic group of matrices (LinearAlgebra/SymplecticGroup.lean), the symplectic Lie algebra (Algebra/Lie/Classical.lean) and symplectic complements in inner product spaces (Analysis/InnerProductSpace/StandardSubspace.lean) — nothing about symplectic forms on real vector spaces or Hamiltonian vector fields. The only Mathlib ingredients used are generic facts (`ContDiff.comp`, `ContinuousLinearMap.contDiff` for continuous linear equivalences, `ContDiff.fderiv_right`), which do not carry the content of the statement. Hence no duplicate or single-declaration special case was found.
